chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you place your forehead upon a mound, do not raise it, but drag it upon the ground.'

key_terms.نَبَكَةٍ: a small mound or raised surface

ai.seo_question: How should one perform the prostration (sajdah) if placing the forehead on a raised surface?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the physical manifestation of humility (khushu') in sajdah by instructing the worshiper to drag the forehead forward rather than lifting it vertically, a practice rooted in the Prophet's tradition. Shia scholars highlight this detail as a means to ensure full contact with the ground, symbolizing complete submission to Allah, and distinguish it from mere mechanical compliance. The instruction reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the spiritual etiquette (adab) of prayer, where physical actions mirror inner devotion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you place your forehead upon a mound, so do not raise it, but drag it upon the ground (towards the place of Sajdah’).
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If you place your forehead on an uneven place, do not raise it to place on a proper place: instead drag it on the ground.’”
